security_spec.violation_condition: In the legacy CSR module (src/main/scala/xiangshan/backend/fu/CSR.scala:314), mipWMask unconditionally includes bit 5 (STIP) as writable via '((1 << 9) | (1 << 5) | (1 << 1)).U(XLEN.W)' — STIP is always software-writable regardless of menvcfg.STCE. In the new CSR module (MachineLevel.scala:247-257), the gating is correctly implemented: when menvcfg.STCE=1, STIP reads from hardware-generated platformIRP.STIP and writes are ignored; only when menvcfg.STCE=0 does the internal reg.STIP become the read source and accept writes. If the legacy CSR module is instantiated in any build configuration where EXT_SSTC=true (always true per CSRConfig line 65), M-mode software can directly set/clear mip.STIP via CSR write even when menvcfg.STCE=1, bypassing the SstcInterruptGen hardware comparator.
security_spec.summary: STIP writability must be gated by menvcfg.STCE=0 per spec: if stimecmp implemented AND STCE=1, STIP is read-only in mip; legacy CSR module allows unconditional STIP writes, enabling M-mode to inject spurious S-mode timer interrupts bypassing hardware stimecmp comparator

findings.finding: mipWMask unconditionally includes bit 5 (STIP) as writable via '((1 << 9) | (1 << 5) | (1 << 1)).U(XLEN.W)'. No menvcfg.STCE gating exists anywhere in this legacy module. The MaskedRegMap at line 835 writes mipReg with this mask, meaning M-mode software can directly set/clear STIP via CSR write to Mip regardless of menvcfg.STCE. This module is dead code (not instantiated; wrapper/CSR.scala:65 instantiates NewCSR instead), so the risk is only material if this legacy module is resurrected or reused as a template.

MaskedRegMap(Mip, mipReg.asUInt, mipWMask, ...) applies mipWMask as the writable-bit mask for Mip CSR writes, propagating the unconditional STIP writability to the CSR address map. No side-effect callback checks menvcfg.STCE before allowing the write.
findings.snippet: MaskedRegMap(Mip, mipReg.asUInt, mipWMask, MaskedRegMap.NoSideEffect, mipMask, x => (mipWire.asUInt | x) & mipMask),

findings.finding: STIP readout is correctly gated: when menvcfg.STCE=1, regOut.STIP reads from platformIRP.STIP (hardware-generated comparator output); when STCE=0, it reads from internal reg.STIP. Writes are correctly blocked: the 'when' conditional at line 250 gates both direct CSR writes (wen) and alias writes (fromMvip.STIP.valid) on '!this.menvcfg.STCE'. This implements the spec requirement that STIP is read-only when SSTC is enabled.

Hardware comparator correctly guards STIP assertion with menvcfg.STCE: o.STIP is only asserted when 'stime >= stimecmp && menvcfg.STCE'. This ensures hardware-generated STIP is only produced when SSTC is enabled, preventing spurious timer interrupts when STCE=0.
findings.snippet:
o.STIP  := RegEnable(i.stime.bits >= i.stimecmp.rdata && i.menvcfg.STCE, false.B, i.stime.valid || i.stimecmp.wen || i.menvcfg.wen)
o.VSTIP := RegEnable(i.vstime.bits >= i.vstimecmp.rdata && i.henvcfg.STCE, false.B, i.vstime.valid || i.vstimecmp.wen || i.htimedeltaWen || i.menvcfg.wen || i.henvcfg.wen)

findings.finding: Mvip.STIP alias is correctly gated: reads return 0 when menvcfg.STCE=1 (since STIP is hardware-driven and not software-writable), and writes to mip.STIP via the alias path (toMip.STIP.valid) are blocked when STCE=1. This prevents M-mode from using mvip as a backdoor to set STIP when SSTC is active.
findings.snippet:
regOut.STIP := Mux(this.menvcfg.STCE.asBool, 0.U, this.mip.STIP.asBool)
toMip.STIP.valid := wen && !this.menvcfg.STCE.asBool
toMip.STIP.bits := wdata.STIP

findings.finding: The active CSR wrapper correctly instantiates only NewCSR (val csrMod = Module(new NewCSR)), which has the correct STCE-gated STIP handling. The legacy xiangshan.backend.fu.CSR class is never instantiated.
MEnvCfg.STCE field is correctly defined as RW with reset value 1 when EXT_SSTC=true. The reset value of 1 means SSTC is active by default, consistent with the RISC-V privileged spec.

STIP field in InterruptPendingBundle is defined as RO(5), reflecting the spec requirement that STIP bit position 5 is a readable interrupt-pending indicator. The write-gating in MipModule correctly overrides any write attempts.
findings.snippet: val STIP     = RO(5).withDescription("Supervisor timer interrupt pending bit.")
